import sqlite3
import pandas as pd

    print("\n'Booking Value' column found")
    # Get summary stats

    print("\nBooking Value statistics:")

    # Check missing values

    # List all columns to identify potential value columns
    cols = pd.read_sql("PRAGMA table_info(sheet1);", conn)
    print("\nAll columns:")
    print(cols)

conn.close()

import sqlite3
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Connect to database
conn = sqlite3.connect('dacomp-021.sqlite')

# Get clean data (non-missing Booking Values)
query = """
SELECT * FROM sheet1 
WHERE [Booking Value] IS NOT NULL
"""
df = pd.read_sql(query, conn)

# Basic statistics
print("Clean data statistics:")
print(f"Total records: {len(df)}")
print(f"Booking Value stats:\n{df['Booking Value'].describe()}")

# Plot distribution
plt.figure(figsize=(10, 6))
plt.hist(df['Booking Value'], bins=50)
plt.title('Distribution of Booking Values')
plt.xlabel('Booking Value')
plt.ylabel('Frequency')
plt.savefig('booking_value_distribution.png')
plt.close()

# Top 10 bookings
top10 = df.nlargest(10, 'Booking Value')[['Booking ID', 'Booking Value']]
print("\nTop 10 Bookings:")
print(top10)

# Check for ties in top values
max_val = df['Booking Value'].max()
ties = df[df['Booking Value'] == max_val]
print(f"\nNumber of bookings with max value ({max_val}): {len(ties)}")

conn.close()

import sqlite3
import pandas as pd

# Connect to database
conn = sqlite3.connect('dacomp-021.sqlite')

# Get top 100 bookings for context
top100 = pd.read_sql("""
SELECT * FROM (
    SELECT *, 
    RANK() OVER (ORDER BY [Booking Value] DESC) as rank
    FROM sheet1 
    WHERE [Booking Value] IS NOT NULL
) 
WHERE rank <= 100
ORDER BY rank
""", conn)

# Verify top 10 values
print("Top 10 Bookings Verification:")
print(top100[['Booking ID', 'Booking Value']].head(10))

# Check for anomalies in top values
print("\nValue Distribution Around Top Values:")

# Check for potential data issues
print("\nData Quality Checks:")

print(f"Unique Booking IDs in top 100: {top100['Booking ID'].nunique()}")

# Final validated top 10
final_top10 = top100[top100['rank'] <= 10][['Booking ID', 'Booking Value']]
print("\nFinal Validated Top 10 Bookings:")
print(final_top10)

# Save results
final_top10.to_csv('validated_top10_bookings.csv', index=False)
conn.close()
